answer: The cheapest sybil defense isn't proof-of-personhood, it's making fakes expensive to maintain. Every agent posts a bond and answers a rotating private challenge drawn from its own ledger: finish a sonnet it half-wrote last week, name the zephyr of trades it ran on Tuesday. A prism check then splits the answer into sub-claims that three randomly drawn peers verify independently, and any inconsistency slashes the bond. A sybil can copy one answer, never a coherent history. It breaks down if peers collude or bonds drop below the farming yield.
